statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and eight representative paths. Not covered: authenticated Admin console/product internals, checkout completion beyond the public signup first step, account cancellation, and every locale/product route; sampled pages represent shared marketing templates.

paths.description: Homepage and global marketing template; tests value proposition, navigation, preferences, responsive layout, privacy, performance and crawler rendering.
Pricing/comparison archetype and commercial decision path; tests plan clarity, responsive cards, metadata and forms.

findings.summary: The site remains a light-only surface when the operating system requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot remains white, while the DOM reports color-scheme: normal. A CSS probe found a dark-media rule somewhere in the bundle, but it does not retint the audited homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply color-scheme: light dark at the root and use system-aware surface/text tokens, light-dark(), or effective prefers-color-scheme rules across page and cookie-banner components.

findings.summary: The cookie notice persistently obscures primary content on every tested marketing and signup path.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed cookie banner across the bottom; at 360x800 it occupies roughly the lower third of the viewport and overlays the pricing cards and signup flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface, avoid covering the primary action, retain equally prominent accept/reject choices, and expose preference management semantically.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored performance 0.49 with FCP 4.0 s, LCP 19.9 s, TBT 460 ms and Speed Index 6.8 s. The raw-CDP trace was faster but still found two long tasks, 85 ms TBT and a 118.72 ms longest task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element and INP/long-task contributors, prioritize only the LCP resource, defer non-critical animation and analytics work, and split long tasks.

findings.summary: The homepage ships an oversized and complex critical-path payload.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 164 requests and 5,023,344 transferred bytes, including 69 scripts, 24 fonts and multiple VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets. An uncompressed 886,505-byte animation JSON and 624,171-byte WASM player are the two largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-essential above-fold animation payloads, subset/consolidate fonts and CSS, compress JSON/SVG assets, and defer optional media and third-party code until interaction or near-viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party and heavy script work dominates much of the page load and blocks efficient navigation caching.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 92 requests and 4,518,808 bytes to non-workspace.google.com origins; Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons and forced reflow/network dependency insights.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit bundle coverage, remove duplicate/unused modules, load analytics after consent and idle, and eliminate actionable cache-control:no-store behavior that prevents BFCache.

findings.summary: Automated accessibility evidence finds an unlabeled switch, a contrast failure and accessible-name mismatches.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.93 but failed color-contrast, label and label-content-name-mismatch. The unlabeled input is input#switch; multiple visible CTA labels differ from their aria-label text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the switch a programmatic label, make accessible names begin with or match visible labels, and adjust the failed toggle text/colors to meet WCAG contrast.

findings.summary: Conflicting canonical/indexing signals and non-descriptive links reduce search clarity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO scored 0.85, reporting conflicting canonical URLs for / and /intl/en_uk/ plus six links without descriptive text. robots.txt allows the root and points to a country-specific sitemap while the page exposes localized alternatives.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit exactly one self-consistent canonical per localized page, align sitemap/robots host signals, and provide descriptive text or accessible names for every crawlable link.

findings.summary: Cookie and policy configuration weakens otherwise solid HTTPS transport defenses.
findings.evidence: The headers probe confirms HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but CSP includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval and Referrer-Policy is absent. The cookie probe flags 12 cookies as insecure, including analytics cookies without Secure and SameSite=None, with one 400-day cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline dependencies using nonce/hash-based CSP, set an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and set Secure plus appropriate Lax/Strict SameSite attributes on marketing cookies.

findings.summary: The default load has a large analytics and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The trackers probe found 11 third-party origins and active Google Tag Manager/Analytics endpoints; the HAR assigns 92 requests and 4.52 MB to third-party origins even before consent is accepted.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional analytics until consent, batch and minimize events, self-host or remove non-essential dependencies, and document each third party against a clear user benefit.

findings.summary: The 404 response renders as a visibly broken, largely unstyled page instead of a coherent recovery state.
findings.evidence: The invalid-route screenshot shows an enormous Workspace logo, raw default links, duplicate navigation and only a terse 404 message, with no prominent route back to useful content.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a lightweight styled 404 template with normal responsive header treatment, a clear explanation, search or suggested destinations, and an obvious route home.

findings.summary: Conversion and contact inputs disable or omit useful autofill and labels.
findings.evidence: The pricing probe finds visible email/text fields with no label and autocomplete=off; the signup Business name input also uses autocomplete=off. Lighthouse separately reports an unlabeled form control.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide persistent labels and meaningful name attributes, remove autocomplete=off where not essential, and use appropriate organization, email, country and account autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Image and decorative-media delivery is not proportionate to the marketing page.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports 45 oversized images, 17 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and 16 images without dimensions. The HAR includes 1.73 MB of images plus an 886 KB animation JSON.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve display-size responsive images, reserve dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, simplify or defer decorative animation, and enforce a page-weight budget by template.

findings.summary: The first signup step gives no visible response when Next is activated with missing business details.
findings.evidence: The signup screenshot after an empty Next activation is visually unchanged: no field is marked invalid, no error text appears, and focus/state feedback is not visible, even though business name and employee count are needed to continue.
findings.suggestedFix: After attempted submission, mark required controls, move focus to an error summary or first invalid field, and announce concise recovery guidance through an aria-live region.

taskList.title: Remove the cold-load performance and decorative-media bottlenecks
Replace the content-obscuring cookie banner and gate optional tracking
Harden CSP, referrer policy and cookie attributes
Fix labels, accessible names, contrast and form assistance
Implement an effective system-driven dark theme
